To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) MSC can be efficiently transduced with retroviruses, 2) MSC can home to tumor and metastatic sites in vivo, 3) MSC transduced with retrovirus encoding prodrug-converter gene are capable of killing tumor cells in vitro and in vivo.
MSC are a good vehicle for gene therapies, as they are not immunogenic, they home to tumors, and they are able to deliver the therapeutic agent to the tumor site.
MSC can be engineered with suicide genes, which can be used for targeted therapy of solid tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of a novel approach to cancer therapy based on MSC-mediated gene delivery of prodrug-converting suicide genes.
development of novel gene therapy strategies based on MSC as cellular vehicles for targeted delivery of therapeutic agents.
the development of a novel therapeutic strategy for treatment of cancer.
